exact_results: A jointly complex-analytic finite-coordinate function yields a real-analytic literal coordinatewise-real fixed-spectator slice; the generic pointwise theorem needs only analyticity at the actual slice image.
The actual complex coordinate Pi norm of a Euclidean vector is bounded above by its Euclidean norm. Equality between the different norms is not assumed.

For D,S>=0 and a fixed actual Euclidean spectator T satisfying S*norm(T)<1, joint complex analyticity on D*norm(spatial Pi block)<1 and S*norm(spectator Pi block)<1 implies real analyticity of the literal slice on the actual Position domain D*norm(X)<1.
For D>0 the slice is real analytic on the actual Euclidean Position ball with center zero and radius inverse D. No dimension-dependent radius loss is introduced.

For A(m,gamma) homogeneous of degree m with actual coefficient L1 <= M*D^m*S^(sum gamma), M,D,S>=0, the actual homogeneousSpectatorSum has these real-slice conclusions with the joint analyticity premise discharged.
semantic_checks: Position is the existing EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 3) alias. Fixed spectators are actual EuclideanSpace Real (Fin d); d=3 specializes to Position.
The generic finite Pi coordinate slice is also provided but does not replace the Euclidean Position theorem.

The coordinate maps are actual continuous linear coordinate projections composed with Complex.ofRealCLM. The complex-to-real step uses analytic scalar restriction and composition, not an assumed slice-analyticity hypothesis.
For Euclidean inputs, coordinate supremum norms are controlled by Euclidean norms with explicit D,S nonnegativity.
The domain conclusions include D=0 and S=0; the inverse-radius ball theorem explicitly requires D>0. Spectator dimension zero is included.
The direct series consumers use the already proved literal pair-index series and anisotropic analyticity theorem. They do not assume reindexing or the desired real conclusion.
